Because it is piece-work tied to a contributor’s own witnessed labour-saving, pre-funded and task-discrete, never pooled or rolled up into a share of enterprise performance, it carries no expectation of profit from the efforts of others and no common enterprise, and so sits outside the perimeter of an investment contract.

Decision D11 — the signer is drawn, not declared

The independent signer becomes a pool draw: the ledger excludes any candidate who has signed for, or been signed by, the requesting estimator on any prior project — closing two-party sandbagging by construction, across project boundaries. Every frozen baseline is benchmarked at freeze against the Replay-visible population of comparable-scope baselines across all projects; an estimate materially outside that peer band auto-escalates to a second, independently drawn signer before the accelerator clock starts. The signer-assignment graph is itself written to Replay as an append-only sub-ledger, so a reciprocal-signing ring becomes a visible pattern rather than a set of individually clean approvals. Nothing settled is undone; a ring found after payout is recorded as a superseding non-qualifying determination governing future settlement only.
coin.witness-example-manila:
Nine Months, Witnessed to Six

Amihan drafts structural retrofits in Manila. A property group retains her to bring forty pre-2010 residential blocks into compliance with a revised seismic code — new load calculations, new reinforcement drawings, a full paper trail for each building. Before she opens a single file, her project lead and an outside code auditor sit down without her and set the frozen baseline: nine months of qualifying work at her local rate, multiple M applied for the specialised certification the job requires. That number is recorded and locked. It is not hers to move, and it is not theirs to move later either.

Amihan adopts an AI-assisted drafting pipeline that cross-checks each drawing against the relevant code clauses in seconds rather than hours and flags discrepancies for her review. It does not draft blind and it does not sign anything — every drawing still carries her personal review and her professional stamp, building by building. What changes is how fast she can move from a flagged discrepancy to a corrected, defensible drawing. Six months later, all forty buildings are done.

The pod reconvenes to witness the claim, and it is a different pod from the one that set the baseline — her project lead, the independent code auditor, and a peer structural engineer from outside her firm, none of whom benefit from either inflating or denying her acceleration. They do not take her word for the six months. They spot-audit a sample of the drawings against the original code clauses, check the defect and revision rate against the firm’s historical average for work of this kind, and confirm nothing was rubber-stamped to hit the clock. The compliance bar was met at the same rigour as the nine-month baseline assumed — it was simply met faster. Only once that is confirmed does the pod certify the three-month delta as ◬.

That delta does not disappear into the property group’s savings. It becomes an acceleration tranche on Amihan’s 웃 ledger, on top of the wage-floor tranche she already earned, unconditionally, for the six months she actually worked. She is paid for nine months of qualifying value at her local rate, in six months of clock time. Nothing about the arithmetic depends on a token appreciating or a market moving; it depends on a locked estimate, a finished body of work, and two independent groups of people who checked it before and after. That is what “witnessed” means in practice, not in principle.

Consider the alternative Amihan did not take: pasting the code into a general chatbot, shipping the output with a light glance, and claiming the same six-month finish. The audit sample would have caught it — a defect rate above the historical baseline, drawings that did not survive spot-checking against the actual clauses, a bar not met. No ◬ mints in that version of events, and it should not. The instrument rewards judgment applied faster, not output generated faster; the witness requirement is the only thing standing between those two, and it is the thing that makes the raise honest enough to put a person’s stamp, and a region’s law, behind it.

— MoT
paper.s15:
§15 · THE FUNDING LOOP ↑ contents

§15   The Funding Loop

Extends §2

There is a woman every family recognizes — the aunt who has finished securing her own years and now watches a nephew build something real in a rented garage. She wants to help. She has helped before, and she remembers how it went: the money arrived as love and settled in as leverage. A cousin funded a bakery and began choosing the bread. She has learned what most people learn quietly — that money given to work becomes a hand on the work, because our instruments cannot tell support from purchase. So she hesitates, and the hesitation is no flaw. It is an accurate reading of the tools she has been offered.

This page hands her a different tool. She may stream her own settled money — money that began as her witnessed hours — into his project, at a pace she alone sets, and what returns is recognition, computed by one published equation. Four terms, a quarter of the weight each: how revenue grew, what it kept as margin, how spending on research grew, and how research intensity stands against a one-third bar. Research occupies two of the four seats on purpose. Her rate per dollar is identical to every other funder’s — the person streaming pennies and the person streaming thousands meet the same figure, so there is no seat to buy and no better deal behind a bigger number.

Run the four lines and the equation says something sharp. A project growing by half, at a seventy percent margin, with research held still, lands at zero point three nine seven one. One with no growth, a sixty percent margin, and research at the bar reaches zero point four zero one zero — slightly ahead — while a healthy project that reinvests clears zero point eight five four nine, more than double either. The formula declines to applaud a harvest dressed as a triumph, in arithmetic short enough to check on paper.

The part that must be said without softening. A loop that moves money attracts the people whose craft is finding the bend in a rule; pretending otherwise would insult both them and you. The defence is not vigilance — vigilance retires. It is the removal of surfaces to grip: one rate for all, nothing tranched, a ceiling that spills into future years rather than paying out, and a single eligible currency — dollars traceable to a person’s own recorded time — so outside capital is not fought at the door; the door simply cannot read its key. A second admission belongs beside it: this loop is a specification. It has been computed, published, argued over. It has not yet faced real money at volume, and a design that survives argument has proven nothing about surviving temptation. The monthly accounting, published when it flatters and when it embarrasses, is where that proof will or will not accumulate.

What you can do today requires no account and no permission. Choose a project you already admire — a company, a lab, the garage down your street. Find its growth, its margin, its research spending, and score it with the four quarter-weighted terms. Whether your admiration survives the arithmetic is the first question this loop was built to ask, and you can ask it tonight — of anyone, including us.

Needs

Recognition that only accumulates is savings, and savings build nothing. A person who has secured their own years and wants to help someone else’s project has, in most systems, exactly one option: give money and hope. Meanwhile the projects that most need support are usually the ones least able to demonstrate why they deserve it, because demonstration is itself expensive and the people who can afford it are rarely the people who need the funding.

Outcomes

A person may redirect their own settlement, dollar by minute, into someone else’s work, and be rewarded on a formula that everyone can compute in advance and nobody can negotiate. Every funder receives the identical rate for the same dollar. There is no preferential tranche. There is no tranche.

Solution

Four terms, equally weighted: revenue growth, operating margin, research spend growth, and research measured against a one-third standard. Research therefore carries two of the four, deliberately. Only settlement-origin dollars are eligible, so external capital is not excluded by a rule but is simply not a valid input to the equation. Rewards above the annual ceiling do not pay out; they enter the rolling floor.

Evidence

The arithmetic makes a statement that is easy to miss unless you run it. A project growing fifty per cent at seventy per cent margin while holding research flat scores zero point three nine seven one. A project growing not at all, at sixty per cent margin, funding research at the one-third standard, scores zero point four zero one zero. Higher growth and higher margin, and less than half the score of a healthy reinvesting project at zero point eight five four nine. That inversion is not a rounding artefact. It is the formula refusing to reward profit taken out of research, which is precisely the behaviour that looks like success on a quarterly report and looks like decline on a twenty-year one. Every term is a number the project already knows about itself, which is why the check costs an evening rather than a research budget.

One seventh of an hour

The buy-in is the same slice of a working life in every country. It is not the same amount of money, and it was never supposed to be.

🔒 The price · class: Immutable

One Seed Token = one local minimum-wage hour ÷ 7.

Eight minutes and thirty-four seconds of minimum-wage work. Everywhere on earth, without exception, checkable by anyone with a clock. The money differs because the world does. The cost in life does not.

Why the anchor went

A dollar is a currency, and anchoring a global unit to one country’s currency makes that country the reference and everyone else the conversion. Dividing by 7 treats every hour identically and no jurisdiction as the origin — Texas now costs $1.04 rather than $1.00, the arithmetic is the same everywhere, and the round dollar of an earlier release was the artefact.

The rate is where you live

The anchor is the posted minimum wage of the region the contributor lives in. Not the country.

Recorded because the previous release got this wrong. It reported four failure classes; three were a country-level question asked of a region-level rule. The rule was right and the test was mine.
● Scope, and what is deliberately unsolved

The rule applies wherever there is a posted hourly minimum wage. Where none exists, an Agreed Wage is to be established — work that belongs to the Global Agreed Standard, an open decision.

Not a gap in the mechanism. A boundary, stated.

The ladder, and why every rung carries the same locks

A Seed Token grants access to a later phase at a higher contribution — and stated plainly, because it is the most exposed thing in this design: early cheap entry that confers the right to join a dearer round later is an option, and options have value. Expectation is the element that decides whether an instrument is a security.

🔒 Every rung, identically locked

Each phase carries the same three properties: non-transferable, no gain of any kind, refund capped at what was contributed. Access to a later phase is therefore access to contribute more — never to gain more.

An option on something with no upside is not a valuable option. That is the whole of the defence, and it must hold at every rung.

Vintages — why nobody gains and the price still rises

A Seed Token is priced by region and year of issue, and that price is frozen for that vintage forever. Texas 2026 is 1.0357 and will still be 1.0357 in 2525.

🔒 Exit, and what it costs
Swap back, at your vintage
Leave whenever you choose. The framework buys the record back at exactly what you contributed — not a sale to a stranger, not a market price.
Leaving is leaving
On exit the membership, the renewal and all interaction with the ecosystem end; nothing is owed in either direction.
Vision • 2525 always receives the original
Whoever holds a vintage, the framework received that vintage’s price once, and it funds global innovation. Acquiring an old vintage later is a collectible act — provenance, not appreciation.

The overage buys years, and nothing else

No cash leaves in the contributor’s direction, ever. What they receive is membership — which pays nothing, returns nothing and appreciates in nothing. A number becomes a newsletter, and a newsletter is not a profit under any definition anywhere.

Every figure here resolves from two published inputs — a statutory minimum wage and a date — through arithmetic anyone can repeat. Perception cannot move any number in this system. In the ecosystem beside this one, value is what the next person believes; here it is what a government published and a clock recorded, and belief is not an input.

● ARX — a different instrument, deliberately kept apart

ARX is a physically-backed token: a chip bonded to a real object, usually a work of art. It is transferable, which the Seed Token is not, and the two must never be described in the same breath.

Every ARX transfer pays 11.1 per cent to the original artist, in perpetuity. One ninth — the same fraction as the replacement gate in §13. The chip tracks ownership so the artist is paid on every onward sale rather than only the first — the transaction art has always lost.

⚠ What the token still is not

Repricing changes nothing else. The token is not 웃, does not mint 웃, does not convert to 웃, and carries no governance weight whatsoever. It remains non-transferable, refundable only up to what was contributed, and attached to no gain of any kind. 웃 is earned by contributed time and by nothing else.

Named plainly, because a reviewer asked for the misreadings in writing. It is not an investment contract — there is no gain to expect, structurally, in any state of the world. It is not a governance token — it carries no vote, no weight and no say, by any route. It is not an appreciating asset — a vintage price is frozen at issue and never moves again. It is not a membership NFT with upside — the membership pays nothing, and any overage converts into more of that nothing.
fund.membership:
The key and the door

A slice of an hour buys the right to buy a year. The year buys you nothing except staying informed — and that is the point, not a shortfall.

Needs

A framework funded one contribution at a time has a problem: one token, once, does not fund anything twice. Contribution that arrives as a single gesture and never returns cannot refuel innovation, and a treasury that only drains is a countdown dressed as a plan.

The obvious fix is the one that destroys everything upstream. A token that entitles you to a share of reserves and is sold on an expectation of gain is a profit interest in a common enterprise. That is the definition regulators apply, and it would put §16 and all ten jurisdictions at risk to solve a cash-flow problem.

Outcomes

Two instruments, and the second one promises nothing at all.

 🌱 Seed Token📧 Membership
Price1/7 of a local minimum-wage hour, once, everpriced separately, per year
Cost in time8m 34s, everywhereset per region
Termpermanent365 days, or 366 in a leap year
What it isthe record that you seeded thisstaying in the loop
What it grantsthe right to buy a membership, nothing elsenews and updates to Vision • 2525
Gain attachednonenone
Reserve claim at shutdownyes — §7none
Mints 웃nono
The token is a key. The membership is the door. Nobody is sold a key on the promise of what is behind the door — and behind the door is a newsletter, not a return.

The recurring money attaches to the instrument with no claim on reserves and no gain of any kind. The reserve claim attaches to the instrument that is never sold on a return. Separated, both survive. Merged, neither does.

Solution
🔒 No gain attached — locked

A membership pays nothing, returns nothing, appreciates in nothing and owes the member nothing. Not a yield. Not a multiple. Not a measured benefit floor. Not a claim on reserves, revenue, tokens or anything else.

What it does is keep a person in the loop: each release, what changed, why it changed, which defect was found, which decision is still open. The record every reader can already see, delivered rather than searched for.

An earlier draft proposed a ten-times utility floor. It was withdrawn at release 53 and the reason is worth keeping. Even framed as usefulness rather than money, a promised multiple is a promise, and a promise attached to a recurring payment is the exact shape a regulator looks for. Removing it cost nothing that mattered and removed the last edge anyone could grip. The earlier wording is still readable at release 52.

Membership revenue enters the innovation treasury and funds the next projects on the four-term formula in §15. It does not distribute, does not accrue to anyone personally, and does not touch 웃 — Shield IV, unchanged.

Evidence

The arithmetic is unglamorous and needs no growth story. One token, once, from a million people funds one round and then nothing. A membership renewed annually by the same million funds a round every year, and the treasury stops being a countdown.

⚠ The obvious objection, stated rather than avoided

The document is public, at /Vision-2525/White-Paper, with no login and no account. So why would anyone pay to be told what they can already read for free? The honest answer is that they would not be paying for access. They would be funding the next projects, and the membership is simply the mechanism that makes that recurring instead of one-time. Being kept current without having to check is a small convenience, not a product. If people will not fund something they believe in on those terms, the model fails — and it should, rather than being rescued by attaching a return to it.

Spec-only Payment rails exist and are cited (backend/app/cubes/cube8_tokens/payment_service.py); the local price resolves through the same settlement lookup 웃 already uses (backend/app/core/hi_rates.py). The membership term, the renewal cycle and the update cadence are proposed and unbuilt. The 365/366 rule is stated precisely because a membership that silently loses a day every fourth year is the kind of small dishonesty that tells you what a system is like.

The ladder

The three coins — the heart, the hand, the mind

♡ S.I. — Shared Intent. Volunteered, documented time offered in goodwill to a common goal — one minute given, one ♡. It is the why, and it is amplified when one person’s effort becomes a tool many reuse.

웃 H.I. — Human Intelligence. Time compensated for skill and judgement, denominated in the local minimum wage. It is the how — the coin redeemable directly for cash, earned live by witnessed minutes and never bought.

◬ A.I. — Artificial Intelligence. Time saved or expanded by tools and automation associated with a project — the accelerator coin, the what at scale. It is a recognition record, redeemed through the accelerator and 웃 it triggers, not a separate cash instrument.

The one line that must never blur — Seed is not 웃

The Seed Token is a one-time join price plus a recurring annual subscription of one seventh of a local-minimum-wage hour per year (the Texas vintage, $1.036/yr), non-accruing and non-transferable — exactly one seventh of a local minimum-wage hour, the Texas vintage $7.25 ÷ 7 — exactly that fraction (725/700 of a dollar), whose decimal 1.03571428571429… repeats and no finite figure captures; shown as $1.036 to three decimal places, never a round $1.00. 웃 (H.I.) is a different instrument entirely: it is earned, live, by witnessed time on a project, and can never be purchased. Buying membership buys a seat in the room; it buys no 웃, no vote, and no share. The Seed Token bears the Seed of Life on one side — the sacred geometry the platform is marked by, the emblem of the membership it represents.

The rule that makes the ladder safe

One person’s sovereignty vote is unaffected by which rung they stand on. A seed contributor and a thousand-tier contributor have identical authority: one unweighted vote each, and only because they are people — not because they paid. Remove that rule and the ladder becomes a price list for influence, which is the precise thing nine releases of legal architecture exist to prevent.
fund.escrow:
Fuelling another person’s work with your own minutes

A person may direct their own dollars per minute — drawn from their own settlement, produced by their own witnessed hours — into a specific innovation project. Daily, or per minute, at a rate they set. They are rewarded in recognition, by the same equation that scores the framework itself.

✓ The rule that closes the door to outside capital

Only settlement-origin dollars are eligible — money itself minted from witnessed human hours. External capital is not excluded by a rule anyone must enforce — it is simply not a valid input. An investment firm has no door here, because the only currency this mechanism accepts began as somebody’s time.

The equation — four terms, equally weighted

g = revenue growth Rev / Rev₋ − 1 gp = gross-profit growth GP / GP₋ − 1 oi = operating-income growth OpInc / OpInc₋ − 1 rds = R&D-spend growth R&D / R&D₋ − 1 P = 0.25·g + 0.25·gp + 0.25·oi + 0.25·rds share(p) = own $/min × minutes streamed ÷ total streamed reward(p) = share(p) × P × recognition pool
Four financial signals, equally weighted.

Revenue, gross profit, operating income, and R&D spend each enter once, at one-quarter weight, as growth over the prior year. Operating income, not operating margin — income is what rolls forward, while margin flatters every project expensive to operate. R&D spend enters as investment in the next decade, not a footnote. Profit is what a project keeps; research is what it gives forward.

fund.metrics:
The Qualified Innovation Score — the benchmark for contribution reward

Honor the Past · Measure the Present · Build the Future.

Innovation performance is measured by ONE canonical score: the Qualified Innovation Score (QIS). It benchmarks the framework and each project and supplies the canonical financial-growth input to downstream qualification and incentive policy — never what a membership is worth.

Four auditable facts, always preserved
  • R — Revenue.
  • GP — Gross Profit (Revenue − cost of goods sold), a dollar amount.
  • OI — Operating Income, a dollar amount.
  • QRD — Qualified R&D Spend, a dollar amount.

QIS is derived from these four; it never replaces them.

One-third R&D commitment → Effective R&D

The R&D target is exactly one third of Revenue (R÷3, displayed as 33.333%). Qualified R&D earns 100% recognition to that target and 50% marginal recognition above it: ERD = QRD − ½·max(0, QRD − R÷3).

The one QIS equation — absolute, one scorecard

QIS = (R + GP + OI + ERD) ÷ 4. The same equation measures a Project, a Group of Projects, and the eXeL Portfolio — only the boundary changes; for a group, aggregate the four absolutes first, then ERD, then one QIS (never average QIS). Growth is the absolute difference ΔQIS = QISFuture − QISBasis (ΔQIS% = ΔQIS ÷ QISBasis × 100, only when the Basis is positive). Frozen basis example — R $1,111,111 · GP $333,333 · OI $111,111 · QRD $100,000 — gives QIS = $413,888.75; the twelve regression vectors and ten invariants are locked in docs/QIS_CANONICAL_SPEC.md.

Evidence → Measurement → Qualification → Incentive

The layers stay separate: the four facts are Evidence; ERD→QIS→ΔQIS→ΔQIS% is Measurement; Qualification decides; Incentive policy acts last. QIS itself creates no recognition, 웃, ◬, 🎁 Bonus, 🏠 Livelihood, compensation, or ownership. Under the current qualified-incentive policy, ΔQIS may size the eligible Reward Pool after qualification, and mints nothing itself. The Accelerator’s sole input stays the witnessed hours delta (D4).

QIS ≠ Ownership

QIS does not create, promise, issue, allocate, or vest ownership. If an ownership incentive is ever authorized, ΔQIS and ΔQIS% are its sole growth measurements; eligibility, issuance, vesting, governance, taxation, securities compliance, qualification and Human Authority stay separate layers.
fund.reward:
The QIS reward, in plain terms

How innovation growth pays people. The Reward Pool is sized by ΔQIS — the absolute growth in the project’s Qualified Innovation Score (§18) — not by any separate weighted formula. It is distinct from the Accelerator (§14, witnessed-hours delta, D4).

Sized by ΔQIS

Take the project’s QIS at the basis and at the later point (each = (R+GP+OI+ERD)÷4), and the Reward Pool is a policy share of the absolute growth ΔQIS = QISFuture − QISBasis, floored at zero so a down period pays no bonus. One equal-weighted scorecard, so growth bought unprofitably scores low.

Wage, not a security

This is earned compensation for qualified work, settled under applicable employment and wage law — not a return on an investment. QIS measures; qualification and Human Authority decide; the Seed stays fixed-value membership.
fund.return:
What a contributor gets back

The operator’s standard: whoever contributes a token fuels Vision 2525 and is expected to gain more than they gave — at minimum, more than the 1/7 of an hour it cost them.

That is the right standard. It needs one precision, and getting it wrong would undo every legal protection in this document.

⚠ Measured, never offered — the line, drawn precisely

Return-on-contribution is a retrospective accountability metric. It is never an inducement, a forecast, a target, or a reason given to anyone for contributing.

The same sentence is safe as an audited historical fact and dangerous as a forward-looking promise. A published expectation of gaining more than was contributed, offered in order to obtain the contribution, supplies the expectation-of-profit limb that Shield IV and the renunciation table exist to remove. This document treats the figure only as an account of what already happened.

The four rules that keep the line

  1. Backward-looking only. Published for periods that have ended. No projection, no forecast, no “expected” figure for a future period, ever.
  2. Never in solicitation. The metric does not appear in any material that asks for a contribution. It lives in the monthly accounting, where results live.
  3. Published when it fails. A ratio below 1.00 is published exactly as prominently as one above it. A metric shown only when flattering is marketing.
  4. No individual attribution. Computed per region, never per contributor. Nobody is told what their contribution returned, because that is the sentence that turns an account into an entitlement.

The metric

return_on_contribution  =   value delivered to contributors and their regions
                            ------------------------------------------------
                                  contribution received, same period

floor      :  1.00        every token returned at least what it cost
reference  :  0.6867 웃  one token = 1/7 hour = 8m 34s, in every jurisdiction
published  :  monthly, per region, in all 33 languages, with the method shown

Corrected at release 56, refined at 57, and CORRECTED AGAIN at 90. r11 printed 0.138. That is 1 ÷ 7.25 — and 7.25 is a wage, not a divisor, so 0.138 was never the right fraction either. The slice is 1 ÷ 7 = 0.1429 of an hour. The same quantity expressed in 웃 is 0.6867, at 4.807 per hour.

Value delivered is not money returned — nothing is paid back, and that is what keeps this outside securities territory. It is what the contribution bought, counted honestly: 웃 settled to contributors in that region; open-licensed output the region now holds and did not pay to license, at replacement cost; education delivered, valued against local tuition for equivalent hours; and infrastructure the region keeps whether or not it keeps contributing.

If the ratio falls below 1.00 for a region, that region is subsidising the framework rather than the other way round, and it is published the month it happens, in that region’s language, without waiting for anyone to notice.

Nobody is promised a return. Everybody is owed an honest account of whether there was one.The line between an accountability metric and an unregistered security

The provenance and settlement layers are separated, and the separation follows the same logic as the three-layer rule: two different jobs should not ride on one instrument.

On-chain hash, off-chain personal data — the division that lets provenance be permanent while keeping the right to erasure intact under GDPR and its analogues.
⚠ The conversion lock

Any mechanism converting recognition into a liquid, externally-tradeable asset re-creates at the conversion point every property the wall was built to eliminate. If 웃 can become a freely traded instrument, then acquiring that instrument becomes a route to whatever 웃 confers. Conversion must be bounded to genuine settlement — a payment to a person for their own recorded contribution — and never a market.

Chain neutrality. A five-hundred-year horizon forbids single-point dependencies, and a specific chain is a single point. The obligation is that governance acts be permanently and independently verifiable; which ledger provides that is Adaptive. QUAI and QI are the current implementation choice, not a constitutional commitment — which is also what makes participation conceivable in jurisdictions where token activity is prohibited outright.

33.333% to research

One third of resources goes to R&D. It is aggressive — tech companies run 10–20% — a system built to innovate should be biased toward what it exists to do.

coin.seed.oneseventh:
One Seventh of an Hour

Ask someone what they would pay to belong, and most people brace for a sales pitch. The Seed answers with an amount so specific it stops sounding like a sales pitch and starts sounding like an admission: one seventh of one hour of the minimum wage where you live. In Austin that is $1.036. In Lagos it is $0.0486. Neither number was chosen to sound impressive. Both were derived the same way, from the same fraction, applied to two very different hours — and that is the entire point.

Why a seventh, and not a tenth, or a whole hour, or a flat dollar everywhere? A flat global price is fairness in disguise for unfairness: a dollar is trivial in Austin and prohibitive in Lagos, so one sticker price would quietly ask more of the poorer contributor and call it equal treatment. A price pegged to a full local hour would make membership itself a day’s labour, heavy enough to gate out exactly the people the Coin exists to include. A seventh sits at the point where the ask is real — you feel it leave your pocket — but never a barrier. It is small enough that refusing it would be strange, and large enough that paying it is a decision, not a reflex. That is the dignity in the number: nobody proves they can afford to join by handing over something that costs them nothing, and nobody sacrifices a day’s wage to say yes.

The choice of a seventh also does quiet legal work. Because the price is a fraction of a wage rather than a fixed face value, it cannot be bid up. There is no auction for Seeds, no secondary market setting a price above the fraction, no scarcity to speculate against. The number moves only when the local minimum wage moves, in the same direction and the same proportion for everyone who joins after. A market price responds to demand for the asset itself; this price responds to nothing but the cost of an hour where the buyer happens to live. That is not how a security is priced. It is a toll calibrated to the road, not to the traffic on it.

Then the Seed asks again, every year, for the same fraction. This detail tells the whole story of what a Seed is not. An investment, once bought, sits and works for the holder, or at minimum does not require a further purchase merely to remain owned. A Seed does the opposite: it lapses unless renewed, and renewal costs exactly what joining cost, recomputed against whatever the local hour is worth that year. Nothing about that structure resembles a stake that appreciates while it is held. It resembles dues — the way a guild, a union, or a commons has always asked its members to keep paying the same small toll to keep their place, not because the place is for sale, but because standing among others who intend the same thing has to be renewed, not banked.

A Seed carries no vote, no share, no claim on anything the Coin’s participants build together, and it cannot be transferred from the person who bought it to anyone else. Buy one in Austin and it belongs to the buyer in Austin; it cannot be gifted, resold, or willed on, because it was never a thing ownable in that sense — it is a standing, renewed, not a deed, held. The 웃 a contributor later earns for an hour honestly worked, and the ♡ a pod records for a contribution that mattered, are the instruments that carry weight in this system. The Seed carries only the right to be present for them: to poll, to be counted, to belong to the room where Shared Intention is being formed. That right costs the same sliver of everyone’s hour, everywhere the Coin is offered — as close as a price can come to saying that no one’s participation is worth more than anyone else’s effort to arrive.

— MoT
coin.seed.value:
The Seed — a membership that keeps its value

The Seed is a fixed-value membership token. It is bought once at one seventh of a local minimum-wage hour (the Texas vintage, $1.036), and it keeps that value — it does not grow, and it is not meant to. Permitting appreciation, transfer, yield, or holder-based economic return could materially increase securities-law risk; the Seed is deliberately designed without those properties.

What it does — membership and loyalty, not investment
  • It unlocks membership. One Seed is the entry credential that lets a person take part — join pods, contribute, and earn 웃 for the work they do.
  • It works like rewards / loyalty points. Holding and using a Seed accrues loyalty standing that unlocks benefits inside the framework — access, standing, and rewards — the way an airline’s miles or a shop’s points card do. It is a balance you spend on benefits, never an asset you sell.
  • It never trades or pays out. The Seed is never priced above its buy-in, never resold, never redeemed for cash, and pays no dividend. Its value is steady by design.

So being early is rewarded the way loyalty is rewarded — in membership, recognition, and benefits that accrue to people who show up — not in a price that climbs. Money is earned only from work you personally perform (웃); the Seed is the membership-and-loyalty layer beside the Trinity (♡ 웃 ◬), never one of the three intelligences and never an investment.
paper.s16:
§16 · THE LEGAL PATHWAY ↑ contents

§16   The Legal Pathway

Extends §4

There is a question you learned to ask before you could name it: will they let me? A licence, a pension, a passport — most of what an adult carries exists because someone agreed to it, and could stop agreeing. One thing never worked that way. Nobody issued you the memory of what you did yesterday, so nobody can revoke it. The distance between those two kinds of holding — the permitted and the simply true — is the whole subject here, because a framework meant to stand in ten legal systems at once decided early which of its parts would be permitted and which true.

The honest answer to ten regimes that distrust one another is not a structure clever enough to satisfy them all — cleverness here shades quickly into evasion. The narrower question: what do they already allow? Three things only: keeping an account of your own work, giving your time freely, and an entity born and funded inside its own borders, obeying its own law. Money breaks somewhere among the ten — so money is made local and severable while the account travels. Where sanctions forbid payment, no payment moves, none is routed sideways; where a technology is prohibited, that layer is switched off rather than costumed — and a framework that cheats one border has told every border what its promises weigh. Refusing to be clever is the load-bearing decision.

Then the arithmetic: what most likely stops everything is not token law but a promise kept casually. Paying earned value out across elected years — one, three, or five — is, in substance, a pension — and history’s pensions failed one way: quietly, owing more than they held. Hence a single inequality, disclosed every month: what is owed may never exceed what is set aside. Take a calculator. The yearly ceiling — nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine — multiplied by seven dollars and twenty-five cents, the founding state’s wage floor, is just under seventy-two and a half thousand dollars: the cost of honouring one person completely. A thousand people, seventy-two and a half million. The hundred-billion ambition becomes a price: between one and a half and three million people fully funded.

Now the part that must not be softened. Law is the slowest layer a civilisation has, and the easiest to capture; a matrix of eleven rows is a map drawn from public statutes, not an approval from anyone. Every row still awaits local counsel. Legislatures amend, and a rule that holds this year can be rewritten by whoever funds next year’s majority. Nothing described here is ratified. The claim is narrower and testable: the irreducible core — a person’s account of their own hours — sits beneath all that contested machinery, so when one jurisdiction closes, exactly one closes.

Test both halves today, without joining anything. Write down one hour you gave, to whom and for what, and notice no office on earth requires a form for it. Then take any guarantee made to you — a pension, a policy, a benefit — and divide what is actually held by what has been promised. If the quotient is less than one, you have just computed the number this entire section exists to keep from hiding, and it is yours now to keep computing.

Needs

A framework that survives in one country is a company. This one has to hold in Austin, China, Brazil, India, Russia, Ukraine, Israel, Iran, the United Arab Emirates and Singapore at the same time, without asking any of them to change anything. Two of them, the United Arab Emirates and Singapore, post no hourly wage floor, so the record reaches them while the pricing rule in §15 does not yet, and without depending on relations between them being good. Any design that requires international agreement has already failed before it starts. The agreement is the hard part, it is not ours to make, and waiting for it is indistinguishable from never beginning.

Outcomes

One pathway that holds everywhere, with the parts that cannot travel switched off locally rather than compromising the whole. Not a lowest common denominator, which would reduce the framework to nothing, but a severable architecture where the core survives even when most of the periphery is unavailable.

Solution

The finding is that the record must be severed from the settlement. All ten permit three things independently: a personal record of what somebody did, time volunteered without compensation. A locally incorporated locally funded entity. Everything else is severable per jurisdiction. In Iran there is no settlement and no routing, and the record still exists. In China the chain layer is simply switched off. The record still exists. What travels between jurisdictions is the smallest possible thing, a record that a person did something, and it travels precisely because it is small enough to be uninteresting to anyone who might otherwise want to stop it.

Evidence

Severability is not a compromise here. It is the only architecture that moves. A design that needs every jurisdiction to permit the full stack is one hostile ruling away from being nothing, and any single government could produce that ruling on any Tuesday. A design where the core is a personal record and everything else is optional cannot be switched off centrally. There is no centre holding the parts that would need switching. This is analysis of publicly available legal structures and not legal advice, no offering is designed here, and the register lists what remains unverified rather than implying the whole is settled.
legal.regimes:
The regulator we will actually meet

Stated once, plainly

“Raises ten dollars for every one” and “not a security” cannot both be true. Substance over form applies in every regime named below. If a return comes from later entrants it is a pyramid, and criminal essentially everywhere. This framework does not design a token sale marketed on appreciation, returns dependent on later participants, sanctions or anti-money-laundering evasion, unlicensed money transmission, or any means of operating where an activity is lawfully prohibited.

Under voluntary citizen funding with no appreciation, no secondary market and no equity, securities law is largely disengaged — while six other regimes engage immediately and are barely mentioned in most comparable documents.

RegimeWhy it engagesMitigation in the design
Charitable solicitationAsking the public for money — per jurisdiction, often per sub-jurisdiction.Shield III: a domestic legal person per region. Monthly full public accounting exceeds most filing floors.
AML / CFTMany small inbound payments; any outbound value transfer.Settlement in local fiat through licensed rails; provenance hashes only, never value custody.
Payments licensingHolding or transmitting others’ funds can constitute money transmission.Settlement structured as payment for recorded contribution via a licensed processor, never as custody of user balances. Requires counsel.
Data protectionContribution records are personal data. Permanence and erasure are in direct tension.Hash on-chain, personal data off-chain and erasable.
Foreign fundingCivic-sector foreign receipts are restricted or criminalised in several target regions.Shield III again. This is the strongest single reason for the federated form.
Pension / end-of-serviceThe guaranteed payout — one, three, or five years at the contributor’s election — is structurally a defined-benefit promise at the longer terms and severance-like at one year.Shield V: the funded reserve. Detailed below — this is the one that matters most.

legal.resilience:
Jurisdictional Resilience & Lawful Portability

The question is not how to escape the law — it is how to ensure that no one actor can capture or halt the framework while every deployment stays fully within the law. Those are opposite things, and the difference matters: capture-resistance is lawful decentralization, not law-avoidance.

No single point of failure — and no single point of control

No single jurisdiction, corporation, investor, founder, infrastructure provider, or technical dependency should be able to capture or stop Vision-2525. Resilience is built, not asserted: lawful decentralization, jurisdictional portability, open standards, Replay and data portability, governance separation, infrastructure redundancy, constitutional rights, and the standing ability to fork and restart. Every deployment remains subject to the applicable law of the place it operates.

Four rights layers, kept separate

Equal human dignity does not require identical institutional authority; the point is that capital or sovereign power cannot buy disproportionate control of the constitutional layer. So four layers are held apart:

  • Human rights — dignity, participation, due process, transparency, portability, exit, privacy, contribution recognition. Not purchasable.
  • Economic rights — contracts, project payments, accelerators, capital repayment. Defined contractually.
  • Governance rights — bounded, role-specific, conflict-ruled, Human-Authority-gated. Not proportional to capital.
  • System rights — fork, Replay, audit, verify, export, restart. Protect continuity against capture.
The ledger is sovereign from its transport

Settlement is adapter-abstracted: the append-only ledger and its Replay are logically sovereign from whatever rail moves the money. A qualified settlement instruction can be carried by a fiat and banking rail, an approved blockchain rail, a Quai/QI-compatible rail, or a future qualified rail — and the framework depends on none of them for its survival, governance, or classification. Reserving the settlement slot without coupling to any one chain is itself an anti-capture mechanism.

Decision D6 — the ledger verified against something it does not control

A record that verifies against nothing but itself has not been verified; it has been asserted twice. Each numbered release now anchors its Replay hash to a public, free, jurisdiction-neutral timestamp service outside operator control — evidence only, no value moves — and an independent mirror of the append-only ledger, held by a non-operator, is counter-signed release by release under the same two-key precedent that governs the off switch. As Shield III’s federated legal persons come online region by region, each becomes an additional independent custodian, so jurisdictional resilience and ledger custody grow from one structure. Tampering that once required deceiving a reader now requires colluding with a public chain that cannot be asked and a second signer never told to look away.

Decision D8 — the 웃 rail is marketplace escrow, not wages

The 웃 rail is a Marketplace Escrow Settlement and the platform is the escrow agent and ledger of record, not an employer. Every engagement settles under an Independent Contributor Agreement between contributor and commissioner: the commissioner pre-funds the task’s known 웃 into ring-fenced escrow, the POD verifies the outcome, and the contributor releases already-vested payout on manual, auto-threshold, up-to-five-times-daily, or scheduled terms. No schedule, tool, or exclusivity is mandated and no direction is exercised over how an outcome is reached, so the design sits outside Earned-Wage-Access regulation, which governs advances against wages accrued under an employer of record — no such relationship exists here. The 9,999 웃 annual boundary stays a settlement and reporting threshold with rollforward, never a wage cap; where local law attaches a statutory wage obligation, the wage-floor tranche honours it on the mandated cadence without disturbing this form. Platform-worker statutes that presume employment from engagement frequency remain a live, jurisdiction-specific question held open pending local counsel.
legal.pension:
The guarantee exposure

⚠ The single most likely reason this gets stopped

It has nothing to do with tokens, crypto, or securities law.

The locked definition says earned value is paid out over an elected term of one, three, or five years, guaranteed. That word is correct, humane, and the whole point of the livelihood design. It is also, in substance, a defined-benefit obligation to individuals — and every developed jurisdiction regulates those heavily, because history is full of guarantees that were not kept.

The current backing is an alert threshold, not a funding rule: ALERT if treasury_coverage_ratio < 0.20 (Token_Governance_Math.md:241-247). A guaranteed stream — up to five years by election — backed by twenty percent reserves is an unfunded retirement promise. It engages ERISA in the United States, CPF in Singapore, EPFO in India, and end-of-service gratuity rules in the UAE — before it engages any securities regulator anywhere.

Shield V: the funded reserve

RULE (Immutable)
  An obligation may be incurred ONLY against reserves actually held.

  committed          = sum of all unpaid instalments already earned
  reserve            = ring-fenced assets, not general treasury
  coverage           = reserve / committed

  coverage >= 1.00   ->  the ceiling may be earned normally
  coverage <  1.00   ->  NEW earning is throttled; earned instalments are unaffected
  coverage <  1.00   ->  the shortfall is PUBLISHED, in every signatory language, that month

Three properties make this the right rule rather than merely a stricter one.

It throttles the future, never the past. A contributor who has earned instalments keeps them under every scenario. Only new earning slows. That is what makes the guarantee a guarantee instead of an aspiration, and it is the difference between this and every pension that failed.

The reserve is ring-fenced. Held separately from operating funds and not available to general expenditure. A reserve a treasury can spend is not a reserve.

Shortfall is disclosed, not managed. Under the project’s own disclosure rule, a coverage ratio below 1.00 is published the month it occurs. A silently underfunded guarantee is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent, and silence is how every historical example of it began.
legal.ramp:
The reserve ramp — and what the guarantee actually costs

Shield V was specified early and stayed unbuilt. It is the largest stoppability exposure in the framework and the one a regulator reaches for first — so it is specified here from a standing start, with the arithmetic run on real numbers.

The rule, in one line

committed  =  every unpaid instalment already earned by anyone
reserve    =  ring-fenced assets, held separately, not available to operations

RULE (Immutable):   committed  MUST NEVER EXCEED  reserve

headroom(period)  =  reserve  −  committed        ← the most that may be newly earned

Three properties make this the right rule. It throttles the future, never the past — earned instalments are untouchable, only new earning slows. The reserve is ring-fenced — a reserve the treasury can spend is not a reserve. And shortfall is published the month it occurs, in every signatory language, because a silently underfunded guarantee is how every historical example of this began.

legal.eleven:
The eleven — one pathway that holds everywhere

The test is deliberately brutal: Austin and the wider United States, China, Brazil, India, Russia, Ukraine, Israel, Iran, the United Arab Emirates and Singapore. Several of these will not be in the same room as each other. Two of them cannot lawfully exchange value at all.

⚠ The wrong instinct, named first

The instinct is to design a clever structure that satisfies all eleven at once. That instinct is how projects in this field end up designing sanctions evasion without admitting it to themselves. We do not do that. Where an activity is unlawful in a jurisdiction, it does not happen there, and we say so publicly.

The finding: sever the record from the settlement

Instead of asking what structure satisfies eleven regimes, ask the opposite question — what do all eleven already permit? The intersection is narrow, and it is not empty:

#Permitted in all elevenWhy it survives everywhere
1A natural person may keep a record of their own workIt is information about themselves. No jurisdiction on earth requires a licence for this.
2A natural person may volunteer their timeFreedom of association, protected in every one of the eleven in some form.
3A locally incorporated, locally funded entity may do locally lawful thingsThis is what every company and charity in every country already is.
Everything else — money, tokens, cross-border flows, guaranteed streams — breaks in at least one of the eleven. So everything else must be locally severable.
The consequence

A fearful government can block settlement inside its borders; it cannot block a person keeping a record of their own hours, because that is not an activity anyone licences. Blocking settlement only denies its own citizens a payment their neighbours receive — while the record keeps accruing, visibly, for the day conditions change.

The eleven, row by row

Austin · Texas
